summary: The focused obligation is a preexisting coverage gap: the old harness cannot exercise string validation of an object member.

claims.necessity_reason: A finite input such as {"data":1} supplies a non-string object member. Both source versions support rejecting it through a string member format. The old harness fixes that member's format to o, which performs no string type check, and its other calls provide no equivalent route.

before.requirement: Unpacking an object member with a string format rejects a non-string value.
before.reason: Object lookup passes the member to the format-selected unpacker, whose s case rejects non-strings. The harness instead selects o for the data member.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Object-member lookup passes the selected value to the format-selected unpacker.

after.requirement: Unpacking an object member with a string format rejects a non-string value.
after.reason: The s type check remains supported, while the same harness still selects o for the data member.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Object-member lookup still passes the selected value to the format-selected unpacker.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Fuzzer bytes supply the parsed JSON object and member value.

claims.comparison_reason: The same fixed {s?o} format prevents string validation of the data member on both sides.
